narrative: Material PL1__MCAEDE30 displays lumpy demand with a CV of 1.15 and only 59% non-zero working days, combined with a statistically significant upward demand trend of +0.96 units/day. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.37, mean 4.28 days), with demand variability accounting for 70% of total lead-time demand variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 815 units and order quantity of 2,295 units was selected to achieve 95% service level while respecting the 3,110-unit storage cap — which binds exactly at the recommended policy.
warnings: Storage capacity binds: unconstrained EOQ 2,759 capped to 2,295 (max_storage_units 3,110 minus safety_stock 815). Service level impact is marginal; cost impact is a slight increase in ordering frequency.
Upward demand trend detected (+0.96 units/day). Mean demand estimate may understate future requirements; review policy in 60-90 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) model is appropriate for lumpy, high-CV continuous demand with moderate lead-time variability. It provides a clear trigger (reorder point r=1,558) and fixed replenishment batch (Q=2,295), which is compatible with the MOQ constraint of 1,539 and allows straightforward SAP implementation via MRP reorder-point planning.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 3,110 units binds at the recommended policy (815 + 2,295 = 3,110). Any increase in safety stock (e.g., due to higher demand volatility) would require a corresponding reduction in order quantity, increasing ordering frequency and cost. If the upward trend materialises, storage capacity will become a binding operational constraint within 1-2 quarters.
